body:
## Summary

Closes #10 (re-scoped to the **private→public / publicize** half — see below).

Repository visibility snapshots (preview-registry `isPrivate`, R2 `META` `visibility`) are written server-side by the preview-api at canonical-deploy time. Previously they only refreshed on a push to `main` or a manual dispatch, so flipping a repo private→public on GitHub left the old snapshot in place — a newly-public repo stayed behind the private-site gate until the next deploy.

This adds GitHub Actions' `public` event to `agent-deploy-site-main.yml` so a private→public transition runs the canonical deployment automatically.

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  public:
```

### Why `public:` and not `repository: [publicized, privatized]`

The original approach used `repository: types: [publicized, privatized]`, but `repository` is **not a supported GitHub Actions `on:` trigger** — it is a webhook/App event that Actions silently ignores, so it would never have started a deploy (YAML-valid ≠ recognized event). `public` is the only repository-visibility transition Actions exposes as an `on:` event; it fires on **private→public only** and takes no `types`.

## Scope split

- **private→public (publicize)** — handled here via `public:`. The deploy refreshes the registry/META from GitHub's current visibility, no manual dispatch needed.
- **public→private (privatize)** — has **no native Actions trigger** and needs a different mechanism (org webhook → `repository_dispatch`, a `schedule:` reconciliation job, or a fail-closed server-side flip in the preview-api). Deferred and tracked in **#31**.

Issue #10 was authored around the `repository:` premise; it has been re-scoped to publicize-now, with privatize tracked separately in #31.

## How it satisfies the (re-scoped) acceptance criteria

- **publicized → public site**: `public` triggers the canonical deploy, which refreshes the registry/META from GitHub's current visibility.
- **Existing behavior intact**: `push` to `main` and `workflow_dispatch` are unchanged.
- **Default branch + concurrency preserved**: the `public` event fires against the default-branch ref, so `github.ref` is `refs/heads/main`. The existing guard `if: vars.AGENT_ENABLED != 'false' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` already accepts it, and the `canonical-site-${{ github.ref }}` concurrency group (with `cancel-in-progress`) is shared with pushes to `main`. No guard or concurrency change required; inline comments explain the intent.
- **Documentation**: the trigger and the snapshot-refresh behavior are documented inline. These workflows have no in-repo unit harness, so documentation covers the criterion.

## External dependency

Closing the publicize path assumes the preview-api re-reads GitHub's live visibility on every canonical deploy. Confirmed from this checkout: [`deploy-sepo-site`](https://github.com/self-evolving/diary/blob/main/.github/actions/deploy-sepo-site/action.yml) posts only `{oidc_token, artifact_id, canonical:true}` to `/api/deploy/preview` — it sends **no** visibility field. So the refresh depends entirely on the server re-deriving identity from the OIDC token and re-reading visibility server-side. If the server caches visibility instead, a paired server-side change (outside this repo) is also needed.

## Verification

- Workflow parses as valid YAML; the `on` block exposes `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `public`.
- `public` is a recognized Actions event (unlike the prior `repository` block).

## AI Review Synthesis > Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**. > Requested by @lolipopshock. Inline comment posted and durable memory recorded. Here is the synthesis. --- ## Summary of PR/Issue This PR closes #10, which aims to auto-refresh the canonical deployment when the repository flips public↔private so the preview-registry `isPrivate` and R2 `META` `visibility` snapshots don't go stale (most importantly, so a newly-private repo isn't left publicly served until the next push to `main`). The change adds a single trigger block — `repository: types: [publicized, privatized]` — to `.github/workflows/agent-deploy-site-main.yml`, plus inline comments explaining the guard, concurrency, and exposure-window reasoning. Notably, this exact trigger was proposed verbatim in issue #10 by the human maintainer. The problem is real and the framing is sound, but the chosen mechanism does not work: `repository` is not a supported GitHub Actions `on:` trigger, so the block is silently ignored and the workflow's behavior is unchanged. ## Review The intent, guard/concurrency analysis, and honesty about dependencies are good, but the change rests on an incorrect premise and, as written, does nothing for either acceptance criterion — it needs a rework, and the privatize half needs a design decision because no native trigger exists for it. | Issue | Severity | Description | | -- | -- | -- | | `repository` is not a valid Actions `on:` trigger — silent no-op | BLOCKING | `repository` is a webhook/App event, not an Actions trigger; the block is ignored, so neither `publicized` nor `privatized` ever runs the deploy. Acceptance criteria #1 and #2 are unmet. | | Privatize has no native Actions trigger at all | BLOCKING | `public:` is the only visibility trigger and covers publicize (private→public) only. The public→private case — the one #10 calls most important — is unachievable with any `on:` trigger and needs a redesign. | | Inline comments document a trigger that never fires | WARNING | The added comments describe `repository` event behavior that won't occur, which will mislead future maintainers into thinking visibility refresh is wired up. | | "Exposure window / not fail-closed" is the primary path, not a follow-up | WARNING | For privatize, the lightweight "flip snapshot first" / server-side route is the *only* viable gate; it can't be deferred as an optimization since the full-rebuild path isn't even triggered. | | External server-side dependency correctly flagged | INFO | Criteria #1/#2 assume the preview-api re-reads live GitHub visibility per canonical deploy; unverifiable from this checkout and honestly called out. | | No workflow linting in CI | INFO | An `actionlint` step would have caught the unknown `on:` event cheaply. Optional. | ## Progress - **Sound parts of the PR:** problem framing, the guard analysis (`github.ref == refs/heads/main`), the shared `canonical-site-${{ github.ref }}` concurrency reasoning, the exposure-window write-up, and the external-dependency disclosure are all genuinely good — and the guard/concurrency reasoning becomes *correct* once the trigger is switched to `public:`. - **Preserved behavior:** existing `push`-to-`main` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers are untouched. - **Provenance:** the non-functional `repository:` trigger was proposed in issue #10 itself by the human maintainer; the PR implemented it faithfully. This means the fix likely involves re-scoping the issue, not just patching the branch. - **Inline comment posted:** one new inline comment on `.github/workflows/agent-deploy-site-main.yml` line 19 flagging the invalid trigger and the `public:` correction ([discussion_r3772169257](https://github.com/self-evolving/diary/pull/30#discussion_r3772169257)). No prior inline comments or review threads existed (verified via REST and GraphQL). ## Issue Details
repository is not a valid Actions on: trigger — silent no-op **Cause:** `repository` (with actions like `publicized`/`privatized`) is a GitHub webhook / App event, but it is not in the allow-list of events that can trigger a GitHub Actions workflow. GitHub keeps running the workflow on the recognized `push`/`workflow_dispatch` and effectively ignores the unknown key, so the deploy never fires on a visibility flip. The PR's "parses as valid YAML" verification cannot catch this — YAML validity is not the same as a recognized Actions event schema. **Candidate solutions:** For the publicize case, use the top-level `public:` event (takes no `types`): ```yaml on: push: branches: [main] workflow_dispatch: public: ``` **Comments:** Ref: https://docs.github.com/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows. This defect defeats both acceptance criteria as written.
Privatize has no native Actions trigger at all **Cause:** GitHub Actions exposes `public` (private→public) as its only visibility trigger; there is no `private`/`privatized` counterpart. So even after fixing the publicize half with `public:`, criterion #2 (privatize → gated site) remains unmet by any `on:` trigger. **Candidate solutions:** (repo has no existing precedent for any of these) - Org-level `repository` webhook bridged to a `repository_dispatch` event (a supported trigger) that runs the deploy — requires org-side setup outside this repo. - A scheduled reconciliation job (`schedule:`) that periodically re-reads visibility and redeploys on drift — bounds the exposure window without an event. - A server-side fix in the preview-api (which owns the snapshot) — the most natural, fail-closed home for the "flip snapshot first" behavior. **Comments:** This is a design change, not a patch, and it needs a maintainer choice. Because the `repository:` approach came from issue #10 itself, re-scoping the issue (e.g., "publicize-only via `public:`, privatize tracked separately") is a reasonable outcome.
Inline comments document a trigger that never fires **Cause:** The added comment blocks explain how `repository (publicized/privatized)` events fire against the default branch and share the concurrency group — accurate reasoning for a trigger that doesn't exist here, so it actively misleads. **Candidate solutions:** If the fix moves to `public:`, rewrite the comments to describe the `public` event (the guard/concurrency reasoning then holds) and remove any claim that privatization is covered.
"Exposure window / not fail-closed" is the primary path, not a follow-up **Cause:** The PR frames the multi-minute rebuild exposure window as a tracked follow-up. But since privatize has no trigger, the full-rebuild path it's meant to improve never runs for privatization — so the lightweight "flip snapshot first" / server-side route is the *only* way to actually gate a just-privatized site. **Candidate solutions:** Surface the lightweight visibility-refresh / server-side flip as core scope (a hard dependency for closing #10's privatize criterion), not an optimization footnote.
No workflow linting in CI (optional) **Cause:** Nothing in CI validates workflow event names, which is why an invalid `on:` event passed review. **Candidate solutions:** Add a small `actionlint` step (e.g., in `test-scripts.yml`) to catch unknown/typo'd triggers cheaply. Optional and out of scope for this PR, but this PR is a good argument for it.
## Recommended Next Step `HUMAN_DECISION` — the publicize half has a clean automatable fix (swap to `public:`), but the "more important" privatize half has no native Actions trigger and requires a maintainer to choose a mechanism and/or re-scope issue #10 (which the maintainer authored with the incorrect premise) before further automation; shipping only the partial fix would silently drop a stated acceptance criterion. ## Final Verdict `NEEDS_REWORK` ## Action Items - [ ] Replace the non-functional `repository: types: [publicized, privatized]` trigger with the top-level `public:` event so the publicize case actually deploys. - [ ] Decide and implement (or explicitly defer) the privatize mechanism — org webhook → `repository_dispatch`, scheduled reconciliation, or a server-side visibility flip — since public→private has no native Actions trigger. - [ ] Rewrite the inline workflow comments to describe the `public:` event and stop claiming privatization is covered. - [ ] Update the PR body (and consider re-scoping issue #10) so it no longer presents privatization as handled by this change. - [ ] Confirm the external prerequisite: the preview-api re-reads live GitHub visibility on every canonical deploy (otherwise even the publicize path won't close #10). --- `claude` | `claude-opus-4-8` | `max` | `GitHub Actions 1000019735`

title: Refresh canonical deploy on repository visibility changes
